children: subscribers are spending less time watching the streaming service and opening its app less frequently, raising concerns about slowing engagement as the company faces mounting competition and decelerating revenue growth, Bloomberg News reported.

Internal data show that customers are using Netflix on fewer days each month than they did several years ago, according to people familiar with the figures cited by the newswire. Average viewing time per subscriber has also declined, even as total viewing hours increased slightly during the first half of 2026 because of subscriber growth.

For investors, weakening engagement raises questions about Netflix's ability to sustain subscription price increases, expand advertising revenue and maintain customer loyalty. Although cancellations remain low, declining usage could eventually undermine pricing power and advertising opportunities, particularly as competitors such as Google's
YouTube capture a growing share of television viewing.

The deterioration began after Netflix cracked down on password sharing in 2022, initially leading executives to expect a temporary decline in usage. However, the trend has persisted, prompting concerns that subscribers may be finding less compelling programming or spending more time with competing services.

Netflix shares have fallen about 29% this year amid worries about slowing growth. The company recently reported its third consecutive quarter of decelerating revenue growth and projected another slowdown in the current quarter. It also reduced its annual advertising revenue outlook by approximately $300 million, citing delays in introducing new advertising products.

Third-party data reinforce the concerns. Research firm Apptopia found that the proportion of U.S. Netflix subscribers who didn't open the app increased 16.6% in the third quarter from a year earlier. However, the company's monthly U.S. cancellation rate remains around 2%, the lowest in the streaming industry, according to research firm Antenna.

Netflix has struggled to produce breakout hits and retain audiences for subsequent seasons of existing shows. The company is increasing programming investments and expanding into live sports and podcasts to strengthen engagement. Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos acknowledged this week that U.S. viewership growth has been weaker than management would prefer, although the company continues to perform well internationally.

The engagement concerns have coincided with a management shake-up. Netflix recently dismissed Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria and film chief Dan Lin while eliminating 6% of its workforce. Former Disney executive Peter Rice has been appointed to oversee content strategy as the company seeks to revive audience interest and restore investor confidence.

title: Netflix viewing is said to fall as engagement weakens, raising growth concerns
